body:
The unsafe lines feature highlight lines that contain unsafe operations, i.e. that may cause type errors at runtime.

* Lines 9 and 14 are highlighted as safe because they are declarations of local untyped variables, you can assign anything to them.
* Line 10 is highlighted as safe because the assigned expression is of the same type as the implicitly inferred type of the variable.
* Lines 11 and 15 are highlighted as unsafe because the assigned expression is of a different type than the implicitly inferred type of the variable.
* Line 16 is highlighted as unsafe because after an unsafe operation with an untyped local variable (line 15), the implicitly inferred type is invalidated.

Actually, in this example, all lines should be highlighted as safe because untyped local variables can take any value. We just don't have good control flow analysis. We could track the current type of a local variable at all points in a function. For an untyped or `Variant`-typed local variable, only uses can be unsafe, not assignments.
